topic: the 1904 Olympic marathon -- Fred Lorz rode in a car for 11 miles, and the actual winner was drugged with rat poison
title: The 1904 Olympic Marathon Winner Was Drugged With Rat Poison
description: AI-narrated history commentary: the true story of the chaotic 1904 Olympic marathon, where Fred Lorz rode in a car for part of the race and the actual winner, Thomas Hicks, was fed strychnine -- rat poison -- by his own trainers.

hook_candidates.text: The 1904 Olympic marathon winner crossed the finish line high on rat poison.
You think Olympic doping is a modern problem. The 1904 winner was drugged with actual rat poison.
What happens when a marathon runner rides eleven miles in a car and still gets caught?
In 1904, one Olympic marathon runner rode in a car and another got drugged by his own team.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks modern doping scandals are bad, because they want proof the first one involved actual rat poison.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume winning an actual Olympic marathon never involved rat poison.
closing_comment: Fred Lorz rode eleven miles in a car during that actual Olympic marathon.

sources.note: Confirms Hicks was given strychnine and brandy by his trainers and nearly collapsed at the finish.
Confirms Lorz rode in a car for part of the race and was disqualified for it.

beats.text: **Rat poison** helped one man win an actual Olympic marathon in 1904.

beats.text: The race itself was brutal, run at midday through St. Louis in blistering heat.

beats.text: One runner, Fred Lorz, dropped out exhausted after nine miles.

an old car parked on a dusty road next to a discarded pair of running shoes

beats.text: His manager drove him the next eleven miles in a car instead.
beats.broll_query: a 1904-era open touring car driving down a dusty road with two men inside

beats.text: Lorz hopped out near the finish and jogged in first, waving to the crowd.
beats.broll_query: a vintage runner jogging into a packed 1904 stadium, waving triumphantly at the crowd

beats.text: Bold strategy for a race with actual judges watching.
beats.broll_query: a row of stern-faced 1900s race officials watching from a stadium platform

beats.text: He was disqualified once officials realized what had happened.
beats.broll_query: a 1900s official pointing accusingly at a runner in a crowded vintage stadium

beats.text: Meanwhile the real frontrunner, Thomas Hicks, was fed **strychnine** and brandy by his own trainers.

beats.text: Hicks finished barely conscious and had to be carried across the line by his handlers.

beats.text: Some records say doctors nearly couldn't revive him afterward.
